answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The design leans on per-epoch sampling audit, re-queued for a second panel, no identity may audit its own recruit. Each submission hangs on the whisper of a task receipt, and the pulse is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. What survives to the horizon is a record of labour, not a list of addresses.
